label: Git Fundamentals
desc: How Git actually stores history — the object model, the three areas, and what a branch really is.

subs.label: Distributed vs Centralised VCS
subs.desc: Why every clone holds the full history, and what that buys you over SVN-style tools.

subs.label: Working Directory, Staging, Repository

subs.label: Branches as Pointers

subs.desc: Ignoring untracked files, and why it has no effect on something already committed.

label: Branching & Merging
desc: Combining work from multiple branches, resolving conflicts, and choosing a team workflow.

subs.label: Fast-Forward Merge
subs.desc: When history is a straight line and Git just moves the pointer forward.

subs.label: Three-Way Merge

subs.desc: Never rebase commits others have already pulled, and why it breaks their history.

subs.desc: Rotate first, then purge with filter-repo — why rewriting history alone is not enough.

subs.desc: A host feature, not a Git one — the gate where review and CI attach to the workflow.

subs.label: Remote-Tracking Branches
subs.desc: What origin/main actually is, and how it powers Git's offline story.

subs.label: Protected Branches
subs.desc: Required reviews, status checks and force-push blocks — quality and audit control.

subs.label: Submodules

desc: Reset, revert, stash and the reflog — how to get out of trouble without losing work.

subs.desc: Revert for public history, reset for private — the rule that avoids breaking teammates.

subs.label: Monorepo vs Polyrepo
